$comment: THE CATALOG. Bastion ships with this list and installs NOTHING from it
until someone asks. Every other copy of it is generated from this file by
`make servers` (scripts/generate-servers.mjs), and CI fails if any of them
has drifted.
This file is a STARTING POINT, not a closed list. It used to be the second
thing - v1 spawned manifest-listed servers and nothing else, and that was
called a security property. It was really two properties wearing one coat,
and only one of them was worth keeping:
KEPT      A caller selects a server by NAME, never by path or command
line. The gateway resolves `/s/<profile>/<server>` against the
user's own installed list and 404s on a miss. Nothing that
reaches the gateway can name a binary, so nothing that reaches
the gateway can run one.
DROPPED   That the list itself was fixed at compile time. This bought no
safety the rule above does not already buy - the user was
always the one choosing - and it cost the app the ability to
run any server that was not written by mgcrea.
So the runtime list lives in Application Support and the user edits it:
install an entry from this catalog, or add a custom one by npm package.
A custom entry supplies a package, a binary name and the variables it
reads - never a command line, because `spawn(whatever_you_typed)` is the
thing the KEPT rule above exists to prevent.
Adding an entry HERE: add it below, run `make servers`, review the diff.
Nothing below is free-form - scripts/servers.schema.json is enforced by
the generator before it writes anything.
Field notes, for the fields whose reason is not obvious:
transport     HOW Bastion reaches the server, and the one field that
changes what everything downstream does.
child   an npm package Bastion installs on demand and
runs with the embedded Node, speaking stdio.
`distribution` says whether it is published:
the difference between an entry a stranger can
install and one that only resolves against a
local checkout through dev.json. The
unpublished ones report 'not published' when
installed, which is the honest answer and
better than a spawn that fails later.
remote  an https URL somebody else operates. Nothing is
installed and no process is started, so the
'one process, N clients' half of the app does
not apply - what does is the credential in the
Keychain and the audit line, which is most of
why anyone puts a gateway in front of a server.
A URL here is a fetch(whatever_you_typed)
primitive, the exact shape of the spawn hole
the KEPT rule closes, so RemoteEndpoint refuses
anything but https to a public host - loopback,
private, link-local and the metadata address
included, Bastion's own gateway loudest of all.
dialect       The NEWEST protocol version the server itself speaks, which
is not the one Bastion fronts clients with. Measured, not
assumed, for the published ones: they run
@modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.29 or 1.30, whose
LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION is 2025-11-25, and a live
`initialize` handshake against mcp-shopify negotiates
exactly that. `make dialect` re-measures.
vendor        CHILD ONLY. Who publishes the package: `mgcrea` or
`third-party`. Stated, never inferred from the scope,
because the typo most worth catching is a typo IN the
scope - `@mgcre/mcp-reddit` fails a startsWith test, gets
treated as somebody else's package, and passes. A rule
that reads the scope to decide which rules apply cannot
catch a wrong scope.
`mgcrea` is held to the naming rule below and checked
against its own TypeScript. `third-party` must be
published, derives its localPath from the package name,
cannot declare a boolean (nothing can verify the default),
and is checked against the PUBLISHED TARBALL instead.
It is also what ServerDetail keys its provenance line on.
A third-party child is the higher-trust ask in this app -
not an endpoint Bastion relays to, but code downloaded and
run on the user's machine with a profile's credentials in
its environment - so silence must not read as "ours".
writeGate     The env var that turns destructive tools on. Set per
profile, never globally.
NULL IS A CLAIM, not a shrug. ToolProbe reads it as "every
tool is a read" and stops asking for confirmation, so a
server whose writes are gated by a CLI FLAG must not be
written down as null - Bastion passes no argv, so there is
nothing to set, and saying null would hand a model every
tool unconfirmed. Leave such a server out of the catalog
until `writeTools` can carry it.
writeGateSense  WHICH WAY the gate points, `enables` (the default) or
`disables`. Every server written here names its gate
`*_ALLOW_WRITES` and treats "1" as on; almost nobody else
does. MDB_MCP_READ_ONLY, READONLY and
ALLOW_ONLY_NON_DESTRUCTIVE_TOOLS are all inverted, and the
last one contains the word ALLOW - so no heuristic over the
name can be trusted, and the field is REQUIRED on a
third-party entry that names a gate.
Applied in exactly one place,
`BastionServer.gateValue(allowWrites:)`. Getting it wrong
spawns a server with writes ON while the toggle, the
profile editor and the Activity window all read as off,
which is a failure with no other detector.
writeTools    REMOTE ONLY, and the counterpart to writeGate: a child
gets an env var that switches its destructive tools off,
and a remote server has no environment to set. So the
gate moves to the only thing Bastion controls - what it
forwards. Named tools are absent from tools/list with
writes off, rather than offered and refused, so a model
never plans around a tool it cannot use.
Bastion also gates any tool the server itself annotates
as not read-only, so a mutating tool added after this
list was written is still caught.
SAY THE LIMIT OUT LOUD. This filters what Bastion
forwards; it does not bind the server. Anyone holding the
credential can call the API directly. The real boundary
is the key's own scopes, and the UI has to say so.
gateBypass    Env vars that would turn writes on AROUND the gate. Bastion
forces these to "0" and never lets a profile set them. No
entry needs one today - mcp-tastytrade did, and the
mechanism outlives it because the next server to OR two
variables into one flag will not announce itself.
stateEnv      Env vars naming on-disk state. Redirected into the
profile's own directory, because two profiles sharing one
token file are two identities sharing one login.
callbackEnv   Env vars naming a loopback OAuth callback URL, and the
`format` to build one from, a template over {port}.
First come, first served. The FIRST profile of a server is
left alone, so it keeps the default the server documents
and its own setup instructions stay true. Only a second
profile gets an assigned port - it is a second identity,
it needs its own socket, and Reddit and X allow one
redirect URI per app, so it needs its own app registration
either way.
Assigning to the first profile instead was tried and was
wrong: it invalidated a registration nobody had changed,
to solve a collision that did not exist yet, and the
symptom was `invalid redirect_uri parameter` on a login
that had worked the day before.
Whatever is decided is written down and kept, because a
registration matched byte for byte cannot survive a port
picked afresh on every spawn. A value the user types wins
over either.
authModes     The ways a profile can be credentialed, and `kind` says WHO
does the work. Three answers, and conflating any two of
them is how a button appears that cannot work:
env       The user fills the named variables and Bastion
sends them. The default, and the only kind
that names variables at all.
oauth     REMOTE ONLY. Bastion is the OAuth client:
discovery, dynamic registration, PKCE, and a
token in its own Keychain scope that no tool
can read back. Needs an endpoint to discover
against, which a child has not got.
childOAuth  CHILD ONLY. The server logs ITSELF in - it
owns the client id, opens the browser, catches
its own loopback callback and keeps the refresh
token in its own per-profile state file. Bastion
drives that flow through the server's own tools
(`loginTool`, `statusTool`, `logoutTool`) and
reports what they say, and holds nothing. The
button looks identical to the user; the
custody is the opposite.
env[].header  REMOTE ONLY. A variable's SINK. Every variable used to
land in one place - an environment variable on a child -
and a remote server has no environment, so it lands in a
request header instead. `format` is a template over
{value}, which is what lets STRIPE_SECRET_KEY become
`Authorization: Bearer rk_...` without the profile
holding the word Bearer.
Same profile, same Keychain, same editor, same missing-
variable check. Only the sink differs, which is what
keeps a remote server from being a second app.

servers.summary: App Store Connect API: apps, versions, builds, TestFlight, listings, analytics, sales.

env.name: APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID
env.description: The 10-character API key id.

env.name: APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID
env.description: Issuer UUID from the Keys page.

env.name: APP_STORE_CONNECT_P8
env.description: The .p8 private key, inline PEM. Preferred: Bastion keeps it in the Keychain and never writes it to disk.

env.name: APP_STORE_CONNECT_P8_PATH
env.description: Path to a .p8 file on disk. The legacy shape — it leaves the key readable outside the Keychain.

env.name: APP_STORE_CONNECT_VENDOR_NUMBER
env.description: Vendor number, needed only for sales and finance reports.

env.name: APP_STORE_CONNECT_CONFIG
env.description: Config file path. Bastion points this at the profile's own directory.

env.name: APP_STORE_CONNECT_ALLOW_WRITES
env.description: Enables the mutating tools: version metadata, screenshots, submissions, pricing.

notes: The inline key is why `secret` is a manifest field rather than a UI
guess. `.mcp.json` in mcp-appstore-connect currently holds this key in
plaintext; migrating it into a Bastion profile is the first dogfood
task in the build order.

servers.summary: CloudKit management API: container schema — record types, fields, Development/Production diff and deploy.

env.name: CLOUDKIT_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN
env.description: CloudKit management token, from icloud.developer.apple.com/dashboard/account/tokens — CloudKit Management Tokens. Can rewrite the container's schema; scope it and revoke when done.

env.name: CLOUDKIT_TEAM_ID
env.description: 10-character Apple Developer team id, e.g. 75QE9PRT3V. Also in the app's exportOptions.plist.

env.name: CLOUDKIT_CONTAINER_ID
env.description: Default container, e.g. iCloud.io.mgcrea.Balise, so it need not be passed on every call. cloudkit_list_containers finds it if unset.

env.name: CLOUDKIT_CONFIG
env.description: Config file path. Bastion points this at the profile's own directory.

env.name: CLOUDKIT_MAX_RETRIES
env.description: Retry budget for 429/5xx responses. Defaults to 3.

env.name: CLOUDKIT_ALLOW_WRITES
env.description: Enables cloudkit_deploy_schema and cloudkit_import_schema. Both additionally require confirm: true on every call.

notes: A separate service from App Store Connect, not a feature of it: different
host (api.icloud.apple.com), different credential (a static management
token, not a minted JWT), no field in common. An App Store Connect key
gives no access here and this token gives no access there — which is
the whole reason this is its own server rather than folded into
appstore-connect, where it lived for one commit before the split.
The API is undocumented. Every route was read out of the `cktool` binary
Xcode ships (`strings $(xcrun -f cktool)`); cloudkit_request is a
GET-by-default escape hatch for whatever that reading got wrong. The one
route it refuses even with writes on is the container's environment
reset — wipes all Development data — which is deliberately not a tool
at all, so exposing it through the escape hatch would defeat the point
of leaving it out.
cloudkit_deploy_schema always fetches and returns the pending diff before
promoting Development to Production, and refuses when there is nothing
to deploy. Production is additive-only forever once first deployed — a
field can be added, never removed, renamed or retyped — so that diff is
the one thing worth reading before confirm: true.
Published as @mgcrea/mcp-cloudkit 0.1.0 on 2026-09-04, so a stranger
can install this one. The scope is covered by a min-release-age-exclude
locally, which is the only reason a version this fresh installs at all.

servers.summary: Reddit API: subreddits, posts, comments, search, and the user's own history.

env.name: REDDIT_CLIENT_ID
env.description: App client id. Anonymous app-only reads work without it; anything user-scoped does not.

env.name: REDDIT_CLIENT_SECRET
env.description: App client secret. Empty for an installed app, set for a web or script app.

env.name: REDDIT_USER_AGENT
env.description: platform:app-id:version (by /u/username). Reddit throttles generic agents regardless of rate limit.

env.name: REDDIT_REDIRECT_URI
env.description: Loopback OAuth callback. Per-profile, or two profiles race for one port — and the URL must be registered with the Reddit app.

env.name: REDDIT_TOKEN_PATH
env.description: Where the refresh token is stored. Per-profile, or two profiles share one login.

env.name: REDDIT_ALLOW_WRITES
env.description: Enables posting, commenting and voting.

notes: The clearest case for stateEnv and portEnv. This server logs a user in
over a local callback and keeps the refresh token in a file — both of
which are per-identity, so both must be per-profile.

servers.summary: X (Twitter) API v2: posts, threads, timelines, search, bookmarks, and the Ads API.

env.name: X_BEARER_TOKEN
env.description: App-only bearer token. Reads only; the Ads API rejects it outright.

env.name: X_CLIENT_ID
env.description: OAuth2 client id. Required for a user context, and therefore for writes and for Ads.

env.name: X_CLIENT_SECRET
env.description: OAuth2 client secret, for a confidential client.

env.name: X_REDIRECT_URI
env.description: Loopback OAuth callback. Per-profile, or two profiles race for one port — and the URL must be registered with the X app.

env.name: X_TOKEN_FILE
env.description: Where the user token is stored. Per-profile, or two accounts share one login.

env.name: X_CONFIG
env.description: Config file path. Bastion points this at the profile's own directory.

env.name: X_MONTHLY_BUDGET_USD
env.description: Spend ceiling. X bills per read, so this is a real safety control, not a preference.

env.name: X_ALLOW_WRITES
env.description: Enables posting through the API rather than returning an intent URL.

env.name: X_ADS_ENABLED
env.description: Registers the Ads API tools. Needs a user context.

env.name: X_ADS_ALLOW_WRITES
env.description: Enables campaign mutations. No effect without X_ADS_ENABLED.

notes: Two write gates, not one: X_ALLOW_WRITES governs posting and
X_ADS_ALLOW_WRITES governs spending money. The manifest names the
first as the gate because that is the one the Activity window badges;
the second is an ordinary env entry that a profile sets deliberately.
X_MONTHLY_BUDGET_USD is here for the same reason a write gate is:
on this API a read has a price, so an unbounded profile is a bill.

servers.summary: UniFi Protect: cameras, event history, recordings, snapshots and NVR status.

env.name: UNIFI_PROTECT_HOST
env.description: Console IP or hostname. https:// is assumed and a :port is preserved.

env.name: UNIFI_PROTECT_USERNAME
env.description: Console login. Use a Local-Access-Only account with View Only rights.

env.name: UNIFI_PROTECT_PASSWORD
env.description: That account's password.

env.name: UNIFI_PROTECT_API_KEY
env.description: unifi.ui.com API key. Selects cloud mode, which needs no local account.

env.name: UNIFI_PROTECT_CONSOLE_ID
env.description: Console id from api.ui.com/v1/hosts. Cloud mode only.

env.name: UNIFI_PROTECT_MODE
env.description: cloud or local. Inferred as cloud when a key and a console id are both set.

env.name: UNIFI_PROTECT_TOTP
env.description: 2FA code. Expires in ~30s, so prefer the server's own login tool.

env.name: UNIFI_PROTECT_VERIFY_TLS
env.description: Verify the console certificate. Needs a hostname, not an IP.

env.name: UNIFI_PROTECT_SESSION_FILE
env.description: Cached session, mode 600. Per-profile, or two identities share one session.

env.name: UNIFI_PROTECT_SNAPSHOT_DIR
env.description: Where snapshots and exports are written. Per-profile, or one profile reads another's footage.

env.name: UNIFI_PROTECT_CONFIG
env.description: Config file path. Bastion points this at the profile's own directory.

env.name: UNIFI_PROTECT_MAX_RETRIES
env.description: Retries on 401 / 429 / 5xx. Defaults to 3.

env.name: UNIFI_PROTECT_MAX_DOWNLOAD_BYTES
env.description: Refuse a download larger than this. Defaults to 200000000.

env.name: UNIFI_PROTECT_DEVICE_CACHE_TTL
env.description: Camera id-to-name cache lifetime in seconds. Defaults to 60.

env.name: UNIFI_PROTECT_ALLOW_WRITES
env.description: Registers the mutating tools: recording settings, PTZ, device configuration.

notes: Two auth shapes that are not interchangeable, which is why they are auth
modes rather than a pile of optional variables. A console API key is
refused by the private API this server reads history from, so a LAN-only
deployment genuinely needs a username and password; a cloud key reaches
the same API through api.ui.com and needs no local account at all.
Three state variables, all per-profile. The session file is an identity,
and the snapshot directory is camera footage — sharing either between two
profiles is the leak this app exists to prevent.

servers.summary: UniFi Network API: sites, devices, clients, WLANs, port and firewall configuration.

env.name: UNIFI_HOST
env.description: The console. A pasted browser URL is accepted and split.

env.name: UNIFI_API_KEY
env.description: Settings, Control Plane, Integrations, Create API Key.

env.name: UNIFI_CONSOLE_ID
env.description: Console id from unifi.ui.com. Cloud mode only.

env.name: UNIFI_MODE
env.description: unifios, cloud or classic. Inferred from what is set.

env.name: UNIFI_SITE
env.description: Default site: UUID, legacy name or display name.

env.name: UNIFI_USERNAME
env.description: Legacy tier fallback only. A local admin, not an SSO account.

env.name: UNIFI_PASSWORD
env.description: That admin's password.

env.name: UNIFI_INSECURE_TLS
env.description: Disable certificate verification, for this server only.

env.name: UNIFI_ENABLE_LEGACY
env.description: Registers the unifi_legacy_* tools.

env.name: UNIFI_APP_VERSION
env.description: Pin the controller version instead of probing it at startup.

env.name: UNIFI_PAGE_LIMIT
env.description: Page size. Defaults to 50.

env.name: UNIFI_MAX_PAGES
env.description: Pagination ceiling. Defaults to 20.

env.name: UNIFI_MAX_RETRIES
env.description: Retries on a transient failure. Defaults to 3.

env.name: UNIFI_CONFIG
env.description: Config file path. Bastion points this at the profile's own directory.

env.name: UNIFI_ALLOW_WRITES
env.description: Enables the mutating tools: WLANs, port profiles, firewall rules, device adoption.

notes: The write gate here reaches network configuration, so a profile with it
on can take a site off the air. Two profiles - one read-only for asking
questions, one gated for changes - is the shape this is built for.

servers.summary: Stripe's own remote MCP server: the API surface, plus documentation and knowledge-base search.

env.name: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
env.description: Restricted API key, sent as the bearer token. A restricted key is the right one here: the write gate filters what Bastion forwards, it cannot take back a permission the key already grants.

env.name: STRIPE_ACCOUNT_ID
env.description: Connected account to act on behalf of, sent as Stripe-Account. Stripe does not support OAuth in this mode, so a profile using it must authenticate with a restricted key.

env.name: STRIPE_API_VERSION
env.description: Pin the API version instead of using the account default, sent as Stripe-Version.

notes: REMOTE. This entry used to be a placeholder for @mgcrea/mcp-stripe, a
package that was never written and never published. Stripe operates a
real MCP server, so Bastion fronts that one instead: the part worth
building here was never a Stripe client, it was the runtime underneath
one - identity, credentials in the Keychain, and a record of every call.
The id is unchanged on purpose. Anyone who made a profile against the
placeholder keeps it.
DIALECT MEASURED 2026-08-31, and it is the oldest in this file. A live
handshake negotiates 2025-03-26 - two revisions behind the default an
unmeasured entry would have carried, which is exactly why the default is
never left in place. serverInfo reports stripe-mcp 1.0.0.
WRITE TOOLS ARE TWO LISTS, and the measurement is why. Of the four tools
hidden with writes off, only stripe_api_write is named below; the other
three - stripe_analytics, stripe_implementation_planner and
send_stripe_mcp_feedback - were caught solely by Stripe's own
readOnlyHint:false annotation. A hand-written denylist would have missed
three quarters of them, so the annotation is not a belt-and-braces extra
here, it is the half that works.
create_refund and stripe_report are named below and were NOT offered by
the account this was measured against. Kept rather than deleted: they
are in Stripe's published tool table, an account that exposes them wants
them gated, and a name that is never offered costs nothing.
Money moves through this one, so the gate is not a formality. Prefer a
restricted key scoped to reads and let the profile stay gated off - the
write gate cannot take back a permission the key already grants.

servers.summary: Shopify Admin GraphQL API: products, variants, collections, metafields, locations.

env.name: SHOPIFY_STORE_DOMAIN
env.description: Store handle or *.myshopify.com domain. A bare handle is expanded.

env.name: SHOPIFY_CLIENT_ID
env.description: Custom app client id.

env.name: SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET
env.description: Custom app client secret. Used as the Admin API access token.

env.name: SHOPIFY_API_VERSION
env.description: Admin API version, e.g. 2026-04. Defaults to the server's pinned version.

notes: No write gate because there is no write path: every tool is a read.
That is why the build order takes this one end-to-end first — a bug in
the supervisor or the dialect layer cannot cost anybody data here.

servers.summary: OVHcloud API, focused on Object Storage: containers, objects, policies, regions.

env.name: OVH_ENDPOINT
env.description: Region endpoint: ovh-eu, ovh-ca, ovh-us. Defaults to ovh-eu.

env.name: OVH_CLIENT_ID
env.description: OAuth2 client id.

env.name: OVH_CLIENT_SECRET
env.description: OAuth2 client secret.

env.name: OVH_APPLICATION_KEY
env.description: Application key, from https://eu.api.ovh.com/createToken/.

env.name: OVH_APPLICATION_SECRET
env.description: Application secret.

env.name: OVH_CONSUMER_KEY
env.description: Consumer key, which carries the granted scopes.

env.name: OVH_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.description: A pre-minted access token.

env.name: OVH_CLOUD_PROJECT
env.description: Default public cloud project id, a 32-character hex string.

env.name: OVH_REGION
env.description: Default storage region, e.g. GRA, SBG, UK.

env.name: OVH_ALLOW_WRITES
env.description: Enables uploading, deleting and re-policying objects and containers.

the only one of the three where every part is a secret, which is

servers.summary: Keycloak Admin REST API: realms, clients, users, roles, sessions.

env.name: KEYCLOAK_URL
env.description: Base URL of the Keycloak server, e.g. https://sso.example.com.

env.name: KEYCLOAK_REALM
env.description: Realm to administer. Defaults to master.

env.name: KEYCLOAK_AUTH_REALM
env.description: Realm to authenticate against, when it differs from the one being administered.

env.name: KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID
env.description: Client id. Defaults to admin-cli.

env.name: KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET
env.description: Client secret. Selects the client_credentials grant.

env.name: KEYCLOAK_USERNAME
env.description: Admin username. Selects the password grant.

env.name: KEYCLOAK_PASSWORD
env.description: Admin password.

env.name: KEYCLOAK_ALLOW_WRITES
env.description: Enables creating and modifying realms, clients, users and roles.

notes: The profile split is the whole point here: rgis and ivalis are two
realms on two servers with two admin identities, and a single global
instance could hold only one of them.

servers.summary: npm registry: packages, versions, downloads, advisories, dist-tags, orgs, tokens and trusted publishing.

env.name: NPM_TOKEN
env.description: npm access token. Optional: with none set the server falls back to the token `npm login` wrote to ~/.npmrc. A granular token with 'Bypass 2FA' enabled is refused by every trusted-publisher write.

env.name: NPM_REGISTRY
env.description: Registry to talk to. Defaults to https://registry.npmjs.org, and the .npmrc token is looked up for whichever host this names, never sent to another.

env.name: NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG
env.description: Which .npmrc the fallback token is read from. Unset means the machine's own ~/.npmrc, which every profile would then share.

env.name: NPM_MCP_CONFIG
env.description: Config file path. Bastion already points the default at the profile's own directory; set this only to name a file elsewhere.

env.name: NPM_OTP_MODE
env.description: How the one-time password npm demands on every trusted-publisher call is obtained: web opens npm's confirmation page and waits, static uses NPM_OTP, none refuses with instructions. Defaults to web.

env.name: NPM_OTP
env.description: A one-time password, and the only thing NPM_OTP_MODE=static will start without complaining about. Rarely right: a code lasts about five minutes, so one set at spawn is dead before anything calls a tool.

env.name: NPM_AUTO_OPEN_BROWSER
env.description: Whether the one-time-password flow launches a browser, or only prints the authorization URL.

env.name: NPM_ALLOW_WRITES
env.description: Registers the write tools: publish and unpublish, dist-tags, deprecation, package access, org and team membership, tokens, and trusted-publisher changes.

notes: No auth modes, and not because there is only one credential. This
server starts with NOTHING configured — every packument, search and
advisory read is public — and a mode has to name at least one
variable, which the zero-config path has not got. So the choice is
not a mode: either NPM_TOKEN is set, or the server reads ~/.npmrc.
Which is exactly why NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG is state. HOME is the real
home, so a profile that names no token quietly borrows the machine's
`npm login` — two profiles are then one npm user wearing two names,
and the audit line says which profile called, not who published. A
second identity points this at its own file, or sets NPM_TOKEN.
The writes worth naming are irreversible in npm's own terms, and the
gate is not the only thing standing in front of them: publish and
unpublish both offer a dry run, and everything irreversible also
wants an explicit `confirm: true`. npm demands a fresh one-time
password on every trusted-publisher endpoint, the READ included, so
unattended trust configuration is impossible by construction rather
than by policy.

servers.summary: GitHub's own remote MCP server: repositories, issues, pull requests, Actions, code scanning and Dependabot alerts.

env.name: GITHUB_TOKEN
env.description: Personal access token, sent as the bearer token. Scope it to the repositories you actually want reachable: the write gate filters what Bastion forwards, it cannot take back a permission the token already grants.

notes: REMOTE. GitHub operates this one; Bastion holds the credential and the
audit line and forwards the call.
DIALECT UNMEASURED. Seeded at 2025-11-25, which is what the one endpoint
in this family that answers unauthenticated actually negotiates. Every
other one 401s before it will say, so this number is a starting point and
not a measurement - RemoteInstance logs `dialect drift` on the first real
handshake and Activity shows what was negotiated. Correct this field from
that line. Stripe is the reason the distinction is written down: it was
carried at the default until a handshake proved it two revisions older.
